title: Gate -1 Identity Validation — Board B Shadow-Mode Pilot
type: Read-Only Identity Validation Report — No Content Modifications
purpose: Execute PG-011 (Identity Validation) against all 5 packs. Validate QID format, CorrectChoice presence, pack attribution, and assess whether Gate -1 would have prevented the S320 identity-ambiguity failure.
methodology: Raw-file grep + PowerShell pipeline extraction. No Function constructor or brace-matcher used — all extractions are string-match from raw file content, avoiding DL-020 and DL-029 class errors.

methodology_notes.qid_extraction: Select-String -Pattern '"QuestionID"' + regex replace to extract bare QID values. Sorted, deduplicated, counted.
methodology_notes.cc_extraction: Select-String -Pattern '"CorrectChoice"' + regex replace to extract A-D values. No forward-scan — CC is extracted from the matching line only.
methodology_notes.cross_pack_collision: Hash-set with pack-attribution tracking. All 2,540 QIDs compared across packs.
methodology_notes.pack_attribution: QID prefix matched against expected pack regex. P1B- items checked for presence outside pack_b. P1E- items checked outside pack_e. P1-[A-F]D- checked outside pack_d. P1-[A-F]C items checked outside pack_c.

pack_a.pack_attribution: CLEAN — all QIDs match pack_a prefix (P1-[A-F]-xxx). Zero P1B-/P1E-/P1-[A-F]D-/P1-[A-F]C- prefixes present.
pack_a.notes: Pack A Section E items (P1-E-xxx) correctly match the Pack A regex. These are distinct from Pack E items (P1E-xxx). This is the DL-033 naming distinction — 'Pack A Section E' vs 'Pack E'.

pack_b.pack_attribution: CLEAN — all QIDs match pack_b prefix (P1B-[A-F]-xxx). Zero cross-pack leakage.
pack_b.notes: Pack B stores CorrectChoice BEFORE QuestionID in the JSON object (unlike Packs A/C/D/E). This caused DL-029 forward-scan false positives in prior sessions. Gate -1 uses line-level CC extraction (no forward-scan), so this format quirk has zero impact on identity validation.

pack_c.pack_attribution: CLEAN — all QIDs match pack_c prefix (P1-[A-F]C-xxx). Zero cross-pack leakage. The optional-C regex handles the two-letter section code (AC, BC, CC, DC, EC, FC).
pack_c.notes: Pack C uses dual-block architecture (metadata ChoiceA-D + content Choices.A-D). Per the spec error_handling, both P1-BC-094 and P1-AC-001 patterns are accepted. The regex includes an optional C suffix.

pack_d.pack_attribution: CLEAN — all QIDs match pack_d prefix (P1-[A-F]D-xxx). Zero cross-pack leakage.
pack_d.notes: Pack D uses dual-block architecture same as Pack C. Zero identity issues detected.

pack_e.qid_invalid_reason: Pattern P1-E-R\d{2} does not match expected /^P1E-[A-F]-\d{3}$/. The P1-E-R prefix follows Pack A Section E naming convention (P1-E-xxx) with an R suffix, not Pack E convention (P1E-xxx).
pack_e.cc_missing_note: P1-E-R33 has NO CorrectChoice field in its JSON object. It also lacks Stem and ExplanationCorrect. Only Choices {A,B,C,D} and ExplanationWrong fields are present. This is a structurally incomplete item — likely an authoring artifact or template placeholder that was never completed.
pack_e.cc_distribution_review: 39 of 40 P1-E-R items have valid A-D CorrectChoice; 1 (P1-E-R33) is MISSING
pack_e.pack_attribution: AMBIGUOUS — 40 P1-E-R* items use P1-E- prefix (Pack A Section E naming) rather than P1E- prefix (Pack E naming). Per the DL-033 naming convention: 'Pack E' = file pack_e_corrected.js, QID prefix P1E-; 'Pack A Section E' = within pack_a_corrected.js, QID prefix P1-E-. The P1-E-R* items violate this convention by residing in pack_e with P1-E- prefix.
pack_e.notes: All 40 blocked items are question_state: 'Certified' — meaning they are in the active learner delivery pool but fail identity validation. All are Section E (Internal Controls) items. P1-E-R33 is the most severe case: no CorrectChoice, no Stem, no ExplanationCorrect — a structurally incomplete Certified item. The 40 items are non-sequential review items (R01-R40 with gaps indicating rotation-group authoring). Their presence in pack_e violates file-location naming conventions and the QID format expected by the regex.

aggregate.blocking_reason: 40 items with QID format P1-E-R\d{2} do not match expected Pack E regex /^P1E-[A-F]-\d{3}$/. 1 item (P1-E-R33) additionally lacks CorrectChoice. All 40 are Certified — in active learner pool.

s320_blocked_analysis.question: Would S320 have been blocked if Gate -1 existed?
s320_blocked_analysis.answer: YES — Gate -1 would have prevented the S320 identity-ambiguity failure.

s320_context.what_happened: S320 executed a DL-026 remediation script (s320_complete_remediation.js) targeting Unprocessed canonical seeds in Pack C and Pack D. The script used QID-only targeting via brace-aware extraction. Because template rotation creates 5+ copies of each QID with different CorrectChoice values, the first brace-match grabbed rotation-group variant copies instead of canonical seeds. Result: 0 correct fills in Pack C (variant mismatch prevented matching), fills applied to wrong QID variants in Pack D. Both packs restored from pre-session backups.
s320_context.root_cause: QID-only identity was insufficient to distinguish canonical seeds from rotation-group variants. The script matched the first QID occurrence, but the Unprocessed canonical seed was not always the first occurrence in the file.
s320_context.wasted_effort: Full session remediation executed, 0 effective writes, both packs rolled back. S320 produced zero certification progress.

how_it_would_block.mechanism: Compound-key identity (step 5 of PG-011): QID + CorrectChoice + EW_Pattern + Template_Family + File_Path + VersionID. Each rotation-group variant has a unique compound key because CorrectChoice differs across variants. A scan targeting canonical seeds can resolve the exact identity rather than matching the first string occurrence.
how_it_would_block.impact: Would have identified that the script was targeting variant copies, not canonical seeds, before any writes occurred.

how_it_would_block.mechanism: TemplateFamily classification (step 4 of PG-011): Items with >90% stem Jaccard similarity would be assigned to the same Template_Family. The canonical seed within each family would be identified (lowest EW entropy, or explicit seed flag).
how_it_would_block.impact: Would have surfaced that the items being targeted were NOT the canonical seeds within their rotation groups. Gate -1 outputs would show template_family membership and is_seed flags, allowing the remediation script to target seeds explicitly.

how_it_would_block.mechanism: IdentityKeyResolver.resolveIdentityKey() (step 5): Verifies compound key is globally unique. Variant copies with same QID but different CC would produce different compound keys, making the identity distinction machine-readable.
how_it_would_block.impact: Would have prevented brace-match-first-occurrence targeting. The remediation script would target the specific compound key, not ambiguous QID position.

how_it_would_block.mechanism: IDENTITY_VALID pre-condition (Gate -1 blocks downstream): No downstream scan result is admissible for IDENTITY_BLOCKED items. If identity is ambiguous, remediation cannot proceed.
how_it_would_block.impact: Would have forced identity resolution BEFORE any remediation scripts ran. The identity ambiguity that caused S320's failure would have been surfaced and resolved at Gate -1 rather than discovered after a failed remediation attempt.

gate_neg1_protection.specific_s320_scenario: In S320, the remediation script searched for P1-BC-094 (for example) and matched the first brace-delimited object containing that QID. In a rotation group of 5 variants, the first occurrence could be any variant. Gate -1 would have: (1) classified all 5 variants into a single Template_Family, (2) identified which variant is the canonical seed (Unprocessed state, structurally distinct), (3) required the remediation script to target by compound key, not by QID string match. Result: correct canonical seed targeted.
gate_neg1_protection.confidence: HIGH — the S320 root cause (QID-only targeting in rotation groups) is precisely the class of failure that PG-011 step 5 (compound-key identity) and step 4 (TemplateFamily classification) are designed to prevent.

gate_neg1_spec_compliance.pg011_step1_qid_validation: EXECUTED — all 5 packs validated against pack-specific regexes. Packs A-D pass. Pack E fails on 40 items.
gate_neg1_spec_compliance.pg011_step2_cc_validation: EXECUTED — all 2,540 items checked for CorrectChoice presence and single-character A-D format. 1 item (P1-E-R33) has missing CorrectChoice.
gate_neg1_spec_compliance.pg011_step3_pack_attribution: EXECUTED — cross-pack collision scan confirmed 0 collisions. Pack E has 40 items with Pack A Section E naming convention (P1-E- prefix) in Pack E file — prefix-to-file-location mismatch.
gate_neg1_spec_compliance.pg011_step4_template_family: DEFERRED — TemplateFamily classification requires AM-1 Function Constructor parse (AM-2 at minimum) and Jaccard similarity computation across all 2,540 stems. This is a Gate -1 scan scope that requires the full scan engine, not raw-file grep. This shadow-mode pilot identifies that the data is available; actual classification is done by the PG-011 implementation.
gate_neg1_spec_compliance.pg011_step5_compound_key: DEFERRED — Compound key resolution requires TemplateFamily + CorrectChoice + EW_Pattern extraction per item. This requires AM-1 parse. Shadow-mode pilot confirms no QID-only collision exists across packs; compound-key resolution would only surface within-pack rotation-group identity issues.
gate_neg1_spec_compliance.methodology_limitations: This shadow-mode pilot uses raw-file line-level grep/PowerShell, not AM-1 Function Constructor parse. This is sufficient for steps 1-3 (pattern matching, field presence, cross-pack collision) but not for steps 4-5 (TemplateFamily, compound key). Steps 4-5 require the full scan engine implementation.

governance_impact.certified_pool_exposure: 40 Certified items in Pack E would be flagged IDENTITY_BLOCKED. These are in the active learner delivery pool. P1-E-R33 additionally lacks CorrectChoice — a learner answering this item would see no correct answer defined.
governance_impact.false_positive_assessment: See SESSION204_IDENTITY_BLOCK_REPORT.json for detailed false-positive analysis.
governance_impact.regex_specification_gap: The Pack E regex (/^P1E-[A-F]-\d{3}$/) does not account for the P1-E-R\d{2} review-item naming convention that exists in the production file. If P1-E-R* is a legitimate naming convention for Section E review/remediation items, the regex must be updated to accept it. If P1-E-R* is a naming error, these items need QID renaming.
